name: Media erosion
doc: Hydraulic erosion on the picture: its luma is the ground of a virtual-pipe shallow-water sim, rain and onset floods fall on it, the bass tips the whole picture so the water runs (a direction per phrase, swaying every two bars) and the flow cuts channels into it where it runs fast down a slope (palette strata in the cuts, sandy deposits where it slows), carrying the picture's colours downstream; the picture re-forms at every phrase start. The wet-paper look reads the same flow as water on a sheet: the picture's darks and contours are ink that bleeds where wet, onset drops bloom with tide lines.

in.doc: the picture: the pigment the water carries (core-media.out)

luma.doc: brightness: the ground the water runs over (core-media.luma)

edges.doc: the picture's contours: drawn in heavier ink in the wet-paper look (core-media.edges)

palette.doc: strata in the cuts, the water's depth and foam, the ink tint

look.doc: erosion: lit relief, carved channels, glossy water; wet paper: ink on a sheet

cells.doc: water grid height in cells (width follows the aspect)

relief.doc: height of white over black, in cells: how strongly the picture routes the water

react.doc: how much the bass adds rain and tips the picture

tilt.doc: how far the bass tips the picture (the water runs downhill)

flood.doc: water dropped at a seeded spot on each onset

carve.doc: erosion: how much the running water cuts and carries

evap.doc: how fast the water dries up

resurface.doc: how fast the cuts fill and the picture's colours seep back

reform.doc: how strongly the picture re-forms at the start of each phrase

ink.doc: wet paper: ink on the picture's contours

tint.doc: foam and wet tint from the palette
